reason: E1 supports that Mn forms non-protective oxides in CrMnFeCoNi, and E3 shows CrTaO4-based oxide can be protective in a refractory HEA at 1100 °C. However, no cited evidence supports the claim that sluggish diffusion aids protective oxide formation, nor that reducing Mn and enriching Cr/Ta in the same alloy system leads to CrTaO4 spinel; E2 does not address these specific mechanisms.
premises: Mn forms non-protective oxides in CrMnFeCoNi HEA at high temperature
CrTaO4-based oxide can be protective in refractory HEAs at 1100 °C
Sluggish diffusion in HEAs stabilizes near-surface composition and aids protective oxide formation
Reducing Mn and enriching Cr and Ta promotes CrTaO4 spinel formation
